text:
alex: Heads up - nightly perf showed a ~50% tokens/sec drop on main after the deploy (commit abc123). First noticed at 02:10UTC, seems correlated with higher queueing and lots of tiny batches.

natalie: saw the alert. infra-bot flagged perf/throughput job failing threshold. linking logs in a sec.

infra-bot: [automated] perf/throughput FAILED on commit abc123. Delta vs baseline: -52% tokens/sec. Report: http://ci.internal/perf/174955 - triggered at 02:12UTC

liam: any obvious suspects from recent merges? I remember a kernel selection tweak last week.

shawn: PR 8417 adjusted kernel scoring heuristics to prefer the fused path only when batch_size >= 16. Also changed a prefetch timing in scheduler. Could be interacting badly with smaller client batches.

alex: profiling snapshot (short):
```
GPU time breakdown: memcpy_fallback 68%
Fused-kernel exec 12%
Scheduler idle/queueing 15%
KV cache hitrate: baseline ~92% -> current ~68% for sample workload
Queue length P50->P90 shifted from 1->3 to 2->12
```

natalie: interesting — I also saw PR 8430 touch the KV keyhash salt for cache namespace isolation. If hitrate drops we get fewer coalesced requests -> smaller batches.

liam: quick hypothesis: KV hitrate drop plus kernel scoring change = more fallbacks to memcpy path and smaller batches, compounding token/sec loss.

shawn: can we bisect 8400..8440? Start with disabling kernel-scoring change first or revert locally.

alex: started local runs: revert 8417 only -> memcpy_fallback disappears, tokens/sec returns to ~98% baseline. Revert 8430 only -> KV hitrate recovers partially, tokens/sec -12% (not full -52%).

liam: that matches. Two contributing changes, kernel scoring is the big win for throughput.

natalie: I put a canary hold on the rollout dashboard and pinged the release manager. We should block pushing to prod until hotfix. :warning:

infra-bot: Rollout hold applied to release/2026-03-17 by shawn at 02:30UTC.

shawn: plan: hotfix PR to revert the kernel-scoring heuristic (rollback 8417) + run full perf suite. After stable, follow-up staged KV salt revert + migration plan (notify customers about cache rebuild).

alex: filing hotfix now, attaching perf runs and profiler output. /cc @eng-oncall @product-support

liam: I'll prepare the bisect artifact and smoke tests to validate on dedicated canary cluster. Expect results in ~45m.

natalie: thanks team. we'll coordinate post-hotfix monitoring for KV warmup effects. :thumbsup:

shawn: if hotfix looks good, do a controlled rollout with telemetry flags to monitor memcpy fallback and batch size distribution.

alex: noted. updating the incident tracker with root-cause hypothesis: interaction(kernel-scoring change, kv-keyhash change) -> smaller batches -> kernel fallback to memcpy -> tokens/sec drop.

liam: bisect update at 03:00UTC: hotfix branch (revert 8417) perf run back to baseline; creating PR now.
